title: Choose the workbench layout
question: Which arrangement best keeps writing focused while making navigation clear on both desktop and mobile?

options.label: Editor-led split
options.thesis: Keep the note dominant and the file tree close at hand; on phones, navigation becomes an explicit touch drawer.
options.viewport: Desktop: slim workspace header, compact file tree at left, wide editor at right, one status line. Mobile: editor-first canvas with labeled browse and note actions; no Vim mode indicator or keyboard-only controls.
options.risk: The split needs a deliberate mobile transition or the file tree will feel cramped.

options.label: Rail and context pane
options.thesis: A narrow persistent destination rail separates navigation from the selected file list, leaving the editor to own the remaining width.
options.viewport: Desktop: slim labeled destination rail, contextual file list, editor. Mobile: a single editor canvas with a bottom touch bar for Browse, New note, and Save; Vim controls stay absent.
options.risk: The extra navigation layer could cost space without enough destinations.

options.label: Editor-first canvas
options.thesis: Give writing the whole stage and reveal workspace navigation only when asked, keeping the mobile model consistent with desktop.
options.viewport: Desktop: compact header, full-width editor, file browser as a left overlay. Mobile: the same editor-first canvas, with clear labeled touch actions and no Vim mode affordances.
options.risk: Frequent note switching adds an extra navigation step.
